answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cost cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewal with them cannot meet the objective. Memory c2 records that a prior switch to the low-cost vendor delivered a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, directly relevant to a 14-day transition window. Memory c4 is verified to confirm whether renegotiation with the incumbent could still recover terms without a full switch, but given the incumbent's stated refusal this cycle, negotiation is unlikely to yield in time. Switching primary vendor addresses the cost mandate and the expiring contract in one move. To manage the 94% assembly-line risk with no buffer, the transition should be structured as a staggered handover—new vendor takes an initial partial allocation while the incumbent fulfills the remainder under a short month-to-month extension (analogous to the deferral pattern in memory c5, though that memory is not pulled for verification). This keeps single-source dependency from re-emerging mid-transition. Delivery risk is mitigated by requiring the new vendor to confirm lead-time commitments and initial stock availability before the incumbent contract lapses. No second source is added this cycle; that waits for the next review.
